// Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ Adapter: bridge async ToolHandler -> sync McpToolHandler Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬

/// Adapts a [`Box<dyn ToolHandler>`] (async, returns `ToolResult`) to the
/// sync [`rustre_mcp_server::McpToolHandler`] trait expected by the
/// executor inside [`rustre_mcp_server::RustReMcpServer`].
///
/// The async `call` is driven on the current tokio runtime via
/// `Handle::block_on` (the MCP server's executor is invoked from synchronous
/// dispatch points but always runs inside a tokio runtime Ã¢â‚¬â€ see
/// `run_stdio` / `run_http`).
struct WireToolAdapter {
    name: String,
    inner: Box<dyn rustre_mcp_server::ToolHandler>,
}

impl rustre_mcp_server::McpToolHandler for WireToolAdapter {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }

    fn execute(
        &self,
        params: Value,
    ) -> Result<Value, rustre_mcp_server::McpToolError> {
        // We are called from inside a tokio worker that is in turn driving
        // the rmcp `call_tool` future. Re-entering the *same* runtime via
        // `Handle::block_on` would deadlock (and `block_in_place` only
        // works on the multi-thread flavour, which the umbrella binary
        // happens to use but other embedders may not). Run the async
        // wire-tool body to completion on a tiny dedicated current-thread
        // runtime built in a separate OS thread instead Ã¢â‚¬â€ this is safe
        // regardless of which runtime called us and never re-enters the
        // outer scheduler.
        let inner = &*self.inner;
        let result = std::thread::scope(|s| {
            s.spawn(|| {
                let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
                    .enable_all()
                    .build()
                    .expect("build dedicated current-thread runtime for wire tool");
                rt.block_on(inner.call(params))
            })
            .join()
            .expect("wire-tool worker thread panicked")
        });
        match result {
            Ok(tr) => {
                // Flatten the ToolResult content blocks into a single JSON
                // value. Handlers in this module always emit a single
                // text content block holding a JSON string, so try to
                // re-parse it; fall back to the raw text otherwise.
                if let Some(rustre_mcp_server::ContentBlock::Text { text }) =
                    tr.content.first()
                {
                    if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(text) {
                        return Ok(v);
                    }
                    return Ok(Value::String(text.clone()));
                }
                Ok(serde_json::json!({ "is_error": tr.is_error }))
            }
            Err(e) => Err(rustre_mcp_server::McpToolError::ExecutionFailed(
                e.to_string(),
            )),
        }
    }
}

/// Map a wire-tool [`ToolDefinition`] to a server [`McpToolDef`] in the
/// `Analysis` category (good default Ã¢â‚¬â€ all current wire tools are analysis
/// or triage primitives).
fn wire_def_to_catalog(def: &rustre_mcp_server::ToolDefinition) -> rustre_mcp_server::McpToolDef {
    rustre_mcp_server::McpToolDef::new(
        def.name.clone(),
        def.description.clone(),
        def.input_schema.clone(),
        rustre_mcp_server::ToolCategory::Analysis,
    )
}

/// Install every handler returned by [`all_wire_handlers`] into the given
/// server, registering each one in both the catalog and the executor.
///
/// Callers should invoke this once, before wrapping the inner server in the
/// rmcp facade (`RustREMcpServer::from_inner`), so the freshly added tools
/// are visible to `list_tools`.
pub fn wire_into_server(server: &mut rustre_mcp_server::RustReMcpServer) {
    for (def, handler) in all_wire_handlers() {
        let catalog = wire_def_to_catalog(&def);
        let adapter = WireToolAdapter {
            name: def.name.clone(),
            inner: handler,
        };
        server.register_external_tool(catalog, Box::new(adapter));
    }
}

// Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ survey_binary Ã¢â‚¬â€ aggregator tool Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬

/// One-shot binary triage aggregator.
///
/// Accepts `session_id` (ignored for now Ã¢â‚¬â€ reserved for future session store
/// integration) and `path` (required: on-disk file to load transiently).
/// Calls multiple sub-routines and merges their results into a single JSON
/// object.  Every sub-call is wrapped so that a failure in one step never
/// aborts the overall response Ã¢â‚¬â€ the error string is placed under that key.
pub struct SurveyBinaryTool;

impl SurveyBinaryTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "survey_binary".to_string(),
            description:
                "One-shot binary triage: load a file and merge results from \
                 the loader, import/section tables, string extraction, function \
                 detection, entropy analysis, and call-target scan into a single \
                 JSON object.  Sub-call failures are recorded per-key rather than \
                 aborting the whole response."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "session_id": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Reserved: session identifier (unused Ã¢â‚¬â€ pass path instead)"
                    },
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Absolute path to the binary file to survey"
                    }
                }
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for SurveyBinaryTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        use rustre_analysis_fn::{
            CallTargetCollector, DetectedArch, MemorySlice, detect_functions,
        };
        use rustre_core::address::Address;
        use rustre_triage::{FileKind, StringHeuristics, analyze_section_entropy, detect_file_kind};

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ Resolve path Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        let path = args
            .get("path")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'path'".into()))?;

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ Load the binary Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        let load = rustre_decompiler::load_binary(std::path::Path::new(path))
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("load failed: {e}")))?;

        let data: &[u8] = &load.data;

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ Detect format Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        let file_kind = detect_file_kind(data);

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ loader Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        // Use RichLoadResult fields (already parsed by rustre_decompiler::load_binary)
        // and augment PE files with extra detail via rustre_loader_pe::PeInfo.
        let loader_val: Value = (|| -> Value {
            let base = json!({
                "kind": format!("{file_kind:?}"),
                "format": load.format,
                "arch": load.arch,
                "bits": load.bits,
                "endian": load.endian,
                "entry_point": load.entry_point,
                "base_address": load.base_address,
                "section_count": load.sections.len(),
                "import_count": load.imports.len(),
                "export_count": load.exports.len(),
            });
            // For PE files, attempt to add richer loader data.
            match file_kind {
                FileKind::Pe32
                | FileKind::Pe64
                | FileKind::Exe
                | FileKind::Dll
                | FileKind::Sys => {
                    match rustre_loader_pe::PeInfo::parse(data) {
                        Ok(info) => json!({
                            "kind": format!("{file_kind:?}"),
                            "format": load.format,
                            "arch": format!("{:?}", info.machine),
                            "bits": load.bits,
                            "endian": "little",
                            "entry_point": info.entry_point,
                            "image_base": info.image_base,
                            "is_dll": info.is_dll(),
                            "is_64bit": info.is_64bit(),
                            "checksum": info.checksum,
                            "section_count": info.sections.len(),
                            "import_count": info.imports.len(),
                            "export_count": info.exports.len(),
                        }),
                        Err(e) => {
                            let mut v = base;
                            v["pe_parse_warning"] = json!(e);
                            v
                        }
                    }
                }
                _ => base,
            }
        })();

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ imports Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        let imports_val: Value = (|| -> Value {
            let imports: Vec<Value> = load
                .imports
                .iter()
                .map(|i| {
                    json!({
                        "dll": i.dll,
                        "name": i.name,
                        "addr": i.addr,
                        "ordinal": i.ordinal,
                    })
                })
                .collect();
            json!({
                "count": imports.len(),
                "imports": imports,
            })
        })();

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ sections Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        let sections_val: Value = (|| -> Value {
            let sections: Vec<Value> = load
                .sections
                .iter()
                .map(|s| {
                    json!({
                        "name": s.name,
                        "virtual_addr": s.virtual_addr,
                        "virtual_size": s.virtual_size,
                        "raw_offset": s.raw_offset,
                        "raw_size": s.raw_size,
                        "flags": s.flags,
                    })
                })
                .collect();
            json!({
                "count": sections.len(),
                "sections": sections,
            })
        })();

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ strings_top20 Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        // Each hit is decorated with the computed virtual address (VA) by
        // resolving its file offset against the section table when one is
        // available; on formats with no section info we fall back to
        // `image_base + offset` so the VA field is always populated.
        let strings_val: Value = (|| -> Value {
            let all = StringHeuristics::extract_strings(data, 6);
            let image_base = load.base_address;
            let sections = &load.sections;
            let off_to_va = |off: u64| -> u64 {
                for s in sections {
                    let raw_off = s.raw_offset;
                    let raw_size = s.raw_size;
                    if off >= raw_off && off < raw_off + raw_size {
                        return image_base + s.virtual_addr + (off - raw_off);
                    }
                }
                image_base + off
            };
            let top: Vec<Value> = all
                .iter()
                .take(20)
                .map(|s| {
                    let off = s.offset as u64;
                    json!({
                        "value": s.value,
                        "offset": s.offset,
                        "va": off_to_va(off),
                        "encoding": format!("{:?}", s.encoding),
                    })
                })
                .collect();
            json!({
                "total": all.len(),
                "strings_top20": top,
            })
        })();

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ function_count Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        let function_count_val: Value = (|| -> Value {
            let arch = match &load.arch as &str {
                "x86_64" | "amd64" | "x86-64" => DetectedArch::X86_64,
                "x86" | "i386" | "i686" => DetectedArch::X86_32,
                "arm64" | "aarch64" => DetectedArch::Arm64,
                _ => DetectedArch::Unknown,
            };
            let base = load.base_address;
            let mem = MemorySlice::new(Address::new(base), data);
            let set = detect_functions(arch, &mem);
            json!({
                "function_count": set.functions.len(),
                "arch": load.arch,
            })
        })();

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ entropy_top Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        let entropy_val: Value = (|| -> Value {
            let mut blocks = analyze_section_entropy(data);
            blocks.sort_by(|a, b| b.entropy.partial_cmp(&a.entropy).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
            let top: Vec<Value> = blocks
                .iter()
                .take(10)
                .map(|b| {
                    json!({
                        "name": b.name,
                        "offset": b.offset,
                        "size": b.size,
                        "entropy": b.entropy,
                        "rating": format!("{:?}", b.rating),
                    })
                })
                .collect();
            json!({
                "block_count": blocks.len(),
                "entropy_top": top,
            })
        })();

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ call_targets_count Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        let call_targets_val: Value = (|| -> Value {
            let arch = match &load.arch as &str {
                "x86_64" | "amd64" | "x86-64" => DetectedArch::X86_64,
                "x86" | "i386" | "i686" => DetectedArch::X86_32,
                "arm64" | "aarch64" => DetectedArch::Arm64,
                _ => DetectedArch::Unknown,
            };
            let base = load.base_address;
            let mem = MemorySlice::new(Address::new(base), data);
            let targets = CallTargetCollector::new(arch).collect(&mem);
            json!({ "call_targets_count": targets.len() })
        })();

        // Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ Merge Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬
        let result = json!({
            "path": path,
            "file_size": data.len(),
            "file_kind": format!("{file_kind:?}"),
            "loader": loader_val,
            "imports": imports_val,
            "sections": sections_val,
            "strings_top20": strings_val,
            "function_count": function_count_val,
            "entropy_top": entropy_val,
            "call_targets_count": call_targets_val,
        });

        Ok(ToolResult::text(result.to_string()))
    }
}

// Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ analysis_fn_detect_functions_path Ã¢â‚¬â€ path-based wrapper Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬

/// Path-based wrapper around `rustre_analysis_fn::detect_functions`.
///
/// The existing `analysis_fn_detect_extra` tool only accepts inline byte
/// arrays / hex strings, which is unusable on real binaries.  This tool
/// loads the file with `rustre_decompiler::load_binary`, picks the arch
/// out of the loader report, and emits per-function `(start, end,
/// confidence, source, name)` records that already carry virtual
/// addresses.
pub struct AnalysisFnDetectFunctionsPathTool;

impl AnalysisFnDetectFunctionsPathTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "analysis_fn_detect_functions_path".to_string(),
            description:
                "Detect function boundaries in a binary on disk.  Loads the \
                 file, infers architecture from the loader report, and runs \
                 the full multi-strategy detector.  Returns a list of \
                 functions with virtual addresses, confidence levels, and \
                 the detection source for each one."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Absolute path to the binary file"
                    },
                    "limit": {
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Optional cap on the number of functions returned (default 5000)"
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for AnalysisFnDetectFunctionsPathTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let path = args
            .get("path")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'path'".into()))?;
        let limit = args
            .get("limit")
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|v| v as usize)
            .unwrap_or(5000);

        let load = rustre_decompiler::load_binary(std::path::Path::new(path))
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("load failed: {e}")))?;

        // The whole-load detector iterates every executable section with the
        // correct VA, merges symbol-table hints, and deduplicates. Calling
        // `detect_functions` on a flat MemorySlice over `load.data` would
        // produce nonsense addresses because raw file offsets are not VAs.
        let boundaries = rustre_decompiler::detect_functions_in_load(&load);

        let total = boundaries.len();
        let funcs: Vec<Value> = boundaries
            .iter()
            .take(limit)
            .map(|f| {
                json!({
                    "start": f.start.as_u64(),
                    "end": f.end.map(|e| e.as_u64()),
                    "confidence": format!("{:?}", f.confidence),
                    "source": format!("{:?}", f.source),
                    "name": f.name,
                })
            })
            .collect();

        let result = json!({
            "path": path,
            "arch": load.arch,
            "image_base": load.base_address,
            "function_count": total,
            "returned": funcs.len(),
            "functions": funcs,
        });
        Ok(ToolResult::text(result.to_string()))
    }
}

// Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ analysis_string_scan_path Ã¢â‚¬â€ path-based wrapper Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬

/// Path-based wrapper around `rustre_analysis_string::StringScanner`.
///
/// Loads the binary, iterates the loader's section table, and runs the
/// scanner against each readable section with the correct section VA as
/// `base`, so every emitted `FoundString` carries an accurate virtual
/// address.  Useful for direct cross-referencing with disassembly output.
pub struct AnalysisStringScanPathTool;

impl AnalysisStringScanPathTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "analysis_string_scan_path".to_string(),
            description:
                "Scan a binary on disk for ASCII / UTF-8 / UTF-16 strings.  \
                 Walks the loader section table and reports each hit with \
                 its virtual address, encoding, length and value Ã¢â‚¬â€ \
                 equivalent to IDA's strings window."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Absolute path to the binary file"
                    },
                    "min_length": {
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Minimum character count for a string to be reported (default 5)"
                    },
                    "limit": {
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Maximum number of strings returned (default 10000)"
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for AnalysisStringScanPathTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        use rustre_analysis_string::{StringScanner, StringScannerConfig};
        use rustre_core::address::Address;

        let path = args
            .get("path")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'path'".into()))?;
        let min_length = args
            .get("min_length")
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|v| v as usize)
            .unwrap_or(5);
        let limit = args
            .get("limit")
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|v| v as usize)
            .unwrap_or(10_000);

        let load = rustre_decompiler::load_binary(std::path::Path::new(path))
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("load failed: {e}")))?;

        let image_base = load.base_address;
        let mut cfg = StringScannerConfig::default();
        cfg.min_length = min_length;
        let scanner = StringScanner::new(cfg);

        let mut all = Vec::new();
        if load.sections.is_empty() {
            // No section table Ã¢â‚¬â€ fall back to scanning the whole file as
            // one block based at `image_base`.
            all.extend(scanner.scan(Address::new(image_base), &load.data));
        } else {
            for sec in &load.sections {
                let start = usize::try_from(sec.raw_offset).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
                let size = usize::try_from(sec.raw_size).unwrap_or(0);
                let end = start.saturating_add(size).min(load.data.len());
                if start >= end {
                    continue;
                }
                let va_base = image_base + sec.virtual_addr;
                all.extend(scanner.scan(Address::new(va_base), &load.data[start..end]));
            }
        }
        // Stable order by VA.
        all.sort_by_key(|s| s.address.as_u64());

        let total = all.len();
        let out: Vec<Value> = all
            .into_iter()
            .take(limit)
            .map(|s| {
                json!({
                    "va": s.address.as_u64(),
                    "length": s.length,
                    "encoding": format!("{:?}", s.encoding),
                    "value": s.value,
                })
            })
            .collect();

        let result = json!({
            "path": path,
            "image_base": image_base,
            "total": total,
            "returned": out.len(),
            "strings": out,
        });
        Ok(ToolResult::text(result.to_string()))
    }
}

// Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ analysis_crypto_scan_path Ã¢â‚¬â€ findcrypt with section-resolved VA Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬

/// Path-based findcrypt: scans every loader section for known crypto
/// constants (AES S-box, SHA-1/256/512 IV+K, MD5 IVs, RSA exponents,
/// Curve25519 / NIST primes, ChaCha20 sigma, Ã¢â‚¬Â¦) and reports each hit with
/// its file offset, section-resolved virtual address, endianness, and
/// matched algorithm set. Additionally runs a BigNum / RSA-modulus
/// heuristic that flags long runs of zero bytes followed by high-entropy
/// blocks Ã¢â‚¬â€ typical of embedded RSA keys or DH primes the constant table
/// can't catch.
pub struct AnalysisCryptoScanPathTool;

impl AnalysisCryptoScanPathTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "analysis_crypto_scan_path".to_string(),
            description:
                "Findcrypt-style scan. Loads the binary, walks every \
                 section, matches against the full crypto-constant table \
                 (LE+BE), and additionally flags BigNum / RSA-modulus \
                 candidates via a zero-block heuristic. Each hit carries \
                 a section-resolved VA suitable for cross-reference with \
                 disassembly."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Absolute path to the binary file"
                    },
                    "min_confidence": {
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Filter out constants below this confidence (0..100, default 0)"
                    },
                    "bignum_min_zeros": {
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Minimum run length of zero bytes to flag a BigNum candidate (default 48)"
                    },
                    "limit": {
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Maximum total findings returned (default 5000)"
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for AnalysisCryptoScanPathTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        use rustre_crypto_id::constant_scanner::{ConstSectionInfo, ConstantScanner};

        let path = args
            .get("path")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'path'".into()))?;
        let min_conf = args
            .get("min_confidence")
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|v| v as u8)
            .unwrap_or(0);
        let bignum_min_zeros = args
            .get("bignum_min_zeros")
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|v| v as usize)
            .unwrap_or(48);
        let limit = args
            .get("limit")
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|v| v as usize)
            .unwrap_or(5000);

        let load = rustre_decompiler::load_binary(std::path::Path::new(path))
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("load failed: {e}")))?;

        let sections: Vec<ConstSectionInfo> = load
            .sections
            .iter()
            .map(|s| ConstSectionInfo {
                file_offset: s.raw_offset,
                file_size: s.raw_size,
                virtual_address: load.base_address + s.virtual_addr,
            })
            .collect();

        let mut scanner = ConstantScanner::new();
        scanner.set_min_confidence(min_conf);
        let hits = scanner.scan_with_sections(&load.data, &sections);

        let mut findings: Vec<Value> = hits
            .iter()
            .map(|h| {
                json!({
                    "kind": "constant",
                    "name": h.constant_name,
                    "algorithms": h.algorithms,
                    "constant_type": format!("{:?}", h.constant_type),
                    "endian": format!("{:?}", h.endian),
                    "confidence": h.confidence,
                    "file_offset": h.file_offset,
                    "length": h.length,
                    "va": h.va,
                })
            })
            .collect();

        // BigNum / RSA-modulus heuristic: scan each section for a window
        // that starts with `bignum_min_zeros` consecutive zero bytes
        // immediately preceding a high-entropy Ã¢â€°Â¥64-byte payload. Real RSA
        // moduli embedded as little-endian arrays show exactly this
        // shape; so do DH/ECDH primes encoded with leading zero padding.
        for sec in &load.sections {
            let start = usize::try_from(sec.raw_offset).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
            let size = usize::try_from(sec.raw_size).unwrap_or(0);
            let end = start.saturating_add(size).min(load.data.len());
            if start >= end { continue; }
            let slice = &load.data[start..end];
            let mut i = 0usize;
            while i + bignum_min_zeros + 64 <= slice.len() {
                if slice[i] != 0 { i += 1; continue; }
                let mut zlen = 0usize;
                while i + zlen < slice.len() && slice[i + zlen] == 0 { zlen += 1; }
                if zlen >= bignum_min_zeros {
                    let tail_start = i + zlen;
                    let tail_end = (tail_start + 256).min(slice.len());
                    let tail = &slice[tail_start..tail_end];
                    // Reject tails that are themselves mostly zero or
                    // low-entropy ascii: count distinct nonzero bytes.
                    let mut seen = [false; 256];
                    let mut distinct = 0usize;
                    for &b in tail { if b != 0 && !seen[b as usize] { seen[b as usize] = true; distinct += 1; } }
                    if distinct >= 24 {
                        let file_off = start + i;
                        let va = load.base_address + sec.virtual_addr + i as u64;
                        findings.push(json!({
                            "kind": "bignum_candidate",
                            "name": "BIGNUM_ZERO_PADDED",
                            "algorithms": ["RSA", "DH", "ECDH"],
                            "constant_type": "FieldPrime",
                            "endian": "Neutral",
                            "confidence": 55,
                            "file_offset": file_off,
                            "length": zlen + tail.len(),
                            "va": va,
                            "zero_run": zlen,
                            "tail_distinct_bytes": distinct,
                        }));
                    }
                    i += zlen.max(1);
                } else {
                    i += zlen.max(1);
                }
            }
        }

        let total = findings.len();
        findings.truncate(limit);

        let result = json!({
            "path": path,
            "image_base": load.base_address,
            "section_count": load.sections.len(),
            "total": total,
            "returned": findings.len(),
            "findings": findings,
        });
        Ok(ToolResult::text(result.to_string()))
    }
}

// Re-export the silenced `hex_encode` helper as `pub use` so it is wired in
// via the wire module (avoids a dead-code warning for the import above when
// no future tool consumes it).
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub(crate) fn _ensure_hex_encode_wired() -> String {
    hex_encode(&[0u8])
}

// Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬ forensics_fs artifact detection tools Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬Ã¢â€â‚¬

fn artifact_to_json(a: &rustre_forensics_fs::artifacts::Artifact) -> Value {
    let meta: serde_json::Map<String, Value> = a
        .metadata
        .iter()
        .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), Value::String(v.clone())))
        .collect();
    json!({
        "kind": format!("{:?}", a.kind),
        "path": a.path,
        "description": a.description,
        "confidence": a.confidence,
        "severity": format!("{:?}", a.severity),
        "metadata": Value::Object(meta),
    })
}

fn read_path_or_data(args: &Value) -> Result<(String, Vec<u8>), McpError> {
    let path = args
        .get("path")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'path'".into()))?
        .to_string();
    let data: Vec<u8> = if let Some(d) = args.get("data") {
        if d.is_array() {
            extract_byte_array(args, "data", "data_hex")?
        } else if let Some(hex) = d.as_str() {
            let cleaned: String = hex.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
            (0..cleaned.len()).step_by(2)
                .map(|i| u8::from_str_radix(&cleaned[i..(i+2).min(cleaned.len())], 16)
                    .map_err(|e| McpError::InvalidParams(format!("data hex: {e}"))))
                .collect::<Result<Vec<u8>, _>>()?
        } else {
            Vec::new()
        }
    } else if let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(&path) {
        bytes
    } else {
        Vec::new()
    };
    Ok((path, data))
}

/// Detect Windows Prefetch artifact.
pub struct ForensicsFsDetectPrefetchTool;
impl ForensicsFsDetectPrefetchTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "forensics_fs_detect_prefetch".to_string(),
            description: "Detect Windows Prefetch (.pf/SCCA) artifact from a path and its bytes.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {"type": "string"},
                    "data": {"description": "Optional byte array or hex string; if omitted, read from path"}
                },
                "required": ["path"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for ForensicsFsDetectPrefetchTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let (path, data) = read_path_or_data(&args)?;
        let art = rustre_forensics_fs::artifacts::detect_prefetch(&path, &data);
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "path": path,
            "detected": art.is_some(),
            "artifact": art.as_ref().map(artifact_to_json),
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

// --- Extra rustre-db base-migrations wrappers (appended) --------------------

/// List migrations that provide a `down_sql` field from `rustre_db::base_migrations()`.
pub struct DbBaseMigrationsWithDownSqlTool;

impl DbBaseMigrationsWithDownSqlTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "db_base_migrations_with_down_sql".to_string(),
            description:
                "Return the versions/names of canonical base-schema migrations that \
                 provide a non-empty `down_sql`, from rustre_db::base_migrations()."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({ "type": "object", "properties": {} }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DbBaseMigrationsWithDownSqlTool {
    async fn call(&self, _args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let migs = rustre_db::base_migrations();
        let items: Vec<Value> = migs
            .iter()
            .filter(|m| m.down_sql.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| !s.is_empty()))
            .map(|m| json!({ "version": m.version.0, "name": m.name }))
            .collect();
        Ok(ToolResult::text(
            json!({
                "count":   items.len(),
                "total":   migs.len(),
                "items":   items,
                "source":  "rustre_db::base_migrations",
            })
            .to_string(),
        ))
    }
}

/// Report whether all `version` fields from `rustre_db::base_migrations()` are unique.
pub struct DbBaseMigrationsUniqueVersionsTool;

impl DbBaseMigrationsUniqueVersionsTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "db_base_migrations_unique_versions".to_string(),
            description:
                "Return whether all `version` fields across rustre_db::base_migrations() \
                 are unique, plus any duplicate versions found."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({ "type": "object", "properties": {} }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DbBaseMigrationsUniqueVersionsTool {
    async fn call(&self, _args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let migs = rustre_db::base_migrations();
        let mut seen: std::collections::BTreeMap<u32, u32> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
        for m in &migs {
            *seen.entry(m.version.0).or_insert(0) += 1;
        }
        let dups: Vec<u32> = seen.iter().filter_map(|(v, c)| if *c > 1 { Some(*v) } else { None }).collect();
        Ok(ToolResult::text(
            json!({
                "count":      migs.len(),
                "unique":     dups.is_empty(),
                "duplicates": dups,
                "source":     "rustre_db::base_migrations",
            })
            .to_string(),
        ))
    }
}

/// Sum of `up_sql` + `down_sql` byte lengths across `rustre_db::base_migrations()`.
pub struct DbBaseMigrationsTotalSqlBytesTool;

impl DbBaseMigrationsTotalSqlBytesTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "db_base_migrations_total_sql_bytes".to_string(),
            description:
                "Return the total byte lengths of `up_sql` and `down_sql` across all \
                 canonical base-schema migrations from rustre_db::base_migrations()."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({ "type": "object", "properties": {} }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DbBaseMigrationsTotalSqlBytesTool {
    async fn call(&self, _args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let migs = rustre_db::base_migrations();
        let up_bytes: usize = migs.iter().map(|m| m.up_sql.len()).sum();
        let down_bytes: usize = migs.iter().map(|m| m.down_sql.as_ref().map_or(0, String::len)).sum();
        Ok(ToolResult::text(
            json!({
                "count":       migs.len(),
                "up_bytes":    up_bytes,
                "down_bytes":  down_bytes,
                "total_bytes": up_bytes + down_bytes,
                "source":      "rustre_db::base_migrations",
            })
            .to_string(),
        ))
    }
}

/// Load built-in Ghidra primitive data types and return the catalog.

    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "ghidra_data_type_db_load_builtins".to_string(),
            description: "Load Ghidra primitive types via rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraDataTypeDb::load_builtins and return the catalog count.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({ "type": "object", "properties": {} }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for GhidraDataTypeDbLoadBuiltinsTool {
    async fn call(&self, _args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let mut db = rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraDataTypeDb::new();
        db.load_builtins();
        let names: Vec<&str> = ["void","char","uchar","short","ushort","int","uint","long","ulong","longlong","ulonglong","float","double","pointer"].to_vec();
        let mut present = Vec::new();
        for n in &names {
            if db.get(n).is_some() { present.push(*n); }
        }
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "count": db.count(),
            "types": present,
            "source": "rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraDataTypeDb::load_builtins",
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

        ToolDefinition {
            name: "ghidra_write_script_to_temp".to_string(),
            description: "Write a Ghidra script to a temp file via rustre_decompiler_ghidra::write_script_to_temp.".to_string(),

        }
    }

            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(e.to_string()))?;

            "source": "rustre_decompiler_ghidra::write_script_to_temp",
        }).to_string()))
    }

/// Probe local Ghidra availability status.
pub struct GhidraAvailabilityCheckTool;
impl GhidraAvailabilityCheckTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "ghidra_availability_check".to_string(),
            description: "Probe Ghidra availability via rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraAvailability::check.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({ "type": "object", "properties": {} }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for GhidraAvailabilityCheckTool {
    async fn call(&self, _args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let status = rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraAvailability::check();
        let variant = match &status {
            rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraStatus::Available(_) => "Available",
            rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraStatus::NotFound => "NotFound",
            rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraStatus::InvalidInstall(_) => "InvalidInstall",
        };
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "status": variant,
            "debug": format!("{status:?}"),
            "source": "rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraAvailability::check",
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

                "type": "object",

            parameters: Value::Null,
        }

impl ToolHandler for GhidraDataTypeDbAddTool {

        let category = args.get("category").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("struct").to_string();
        let size_bytes = args.get("size_bytes").and_then(Value::as_u64).unwrap_or(4) as usize;
        let c_repr = args.get("c_repr").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("struct MyType {};").to_string();

        db.add(rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraDataType {
            name: name.clone(), category, size_bytes, c_representation: c_repr,
        });
        let hit = db.get(&name).map(|d| d.c_representation.clone());
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "count": db.count(),
            "c_representation": hit,
            "source": "rustre_decompiler_ghidra::GhidraDataTypeDb::add",
        }).to_string()))
    }

fn callconv_pattern_to_json(p: &rustre_analysis_callconv::CallingConventionPattern) -> Value {
    json!({
        "name":                p.name,
        "arg_registers":       p.arg_registers,
        "fp_arg_registers":    p.fp_arg_registers,
        "retval_registers":    p.retval_registers,
        "callee_saved":        p.callee_saved,
        "caller_saved":        p.caller_saved,
        "stack_alignment":     p.stack_alignment,
        "caller_cleanup":      p.caller_cleanup,
        "hidden_this_ptr":     p.hidden_this_ptr,
        "max_reg_args":        p.max_reg_args,
        "supports_variadic":   p.supports_variadic,
        "shadow_space_bytes":  p.shadow_space_bytes,
    })
}

// --- analysis_string_detect_xor_key ------------------------------------
pub struct AnalysisStringDetectXorKeyTool;
impl AnalysisStringDetectXorKeyTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "analysis_string_detect_xor_key".to_string(),
            description: "Detect single-byte XOR key from hex-encoded data via rustre_analysis_string::detect_xor_key.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": { "hex": { "type": "string", "description": "Hex-encoded input bytes" } },
                "required": ["hex"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for AnalysisStringDetectXorKeyTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let hex = args.get("hex").and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'hex'".into()))?;
        let clean: String = hex.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
        if clean.len() % 2 != 0 {
            return Err(McpError::InvalidParams("hex length must be even".into()));
        }
        let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(clean.len() / 2);
        for i in (0..clean.len()).step_by(2) {
            let byte = u8::from_str_radix(&clean[i..i + 2], 16)
                .map_err(|e| McpError::InvalidParams(format!("bad hex: {e}")))?;
            data.push(byte);
        }
        let key = rustre_analysis_string::detect_xor_key(&data);
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "input_bytes": data.len(),
            "key": key,
            "found": key.is_some(),
            "source": "rustre_analysis_string::detect_xor_key",
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

// --- analysis_string_extract_urls_path ---------------------------------
pub struct AnalysisStringExtractUrlsPathTool;
impl AnalysisStringExtractUrlsPathTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "analysis_string_extract_urls_path".to_string(),
            description: "Scan a binary's sections for strings and extract URLs via rustre_analysis_string::extract_urls.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": { "type": "string" },
                    "min_length": { "type": "integer" },
                    "limit": { "type": "integer" }
                },
                "required": ["path"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for AnalysisStringExtractUrlsPathTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        use rustre_analysis_string::{StringScanner, StringScannerConfig, extract_urls};
        use rustre_core::address::Address;

        let path = args.get("path").and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'path'".into()))?;
        let min_length = args.get("min_length").and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|v| v as usize).unwrap_or(5);
        let limit = args.get("limit").and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|v| v as usize).unwrap_or(1000);

        let load = rustre_decompiler::load_binary(std::path::Path::new(path))
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("load failed: {e}")))?;
        let image_base = load.base_address;
        let mut cfg = StringScannerConfig::default();
        cfg.min_length = min_length;
        let scanner = StringScanner::new(cfg);

        let mut all = Vec::new();
        if load.sections.is_empty() {
            all.extend(scanner.scan(Address::new(image_base), &load.data));
        } else {
            for sec in &load.sections {
                let start = usize::try_from(sec.raw_offset).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
                let size = usize::try_from(sec.raw_size).unwrap_or(0);
                let end = start.saturating_add(size).min(load.data.len());
                if start >= end { continue; }
                let va_base = image_base + sec.virtual_addr;
                all.extend(scanner.scan(Address::new(va_base), &load.data[start..end]));
            }
        }
        let urls = extract_urls(&all);
        let total = urls.len();
        let out: Vec<Value> = urls.into_iter().take(limit).map(|u| {
            json!({
                "url": u.url,
                "scheme": u.scheme,
                "host": u.host,
            })
        }).collect();
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "path": path,
            "total": total,
            "returned": out.len(),
            "urls": out,
            "source": "rustre_analysis_string::extract_urls",
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

impl AnalysisStringStatsPathTool {

    }

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for AnalysisStringStatsPathTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        use rustre_analysis_string::{StringScanner, StringScannerConfig, StringStats};
        use rustre_core::address::Address;

        let path = args.get("path").and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'path'".into()))?;
        let min_length = args.get("min_length").and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|v| v as usize).unwrap_or(5);

        let load = rustre_decompiler::load_binary(std::path::Path::new(path))
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("load failed: {e}")))?;
        let image_base = load.base_address;
        let mut cfg = StringScannerConfig::default();
        cfg.min_length = min_length;
        let scanner = StringScanner::new(cfg);

        let mut all = Vec::new();
        if load.sections.is_empty() {
            all.extend(scanner.scan(Address::new(image_base), &load.data));
        } else {
            for sec in &load.sections {
                let start = usize::try_from(sec.raw_offset).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
                let size = usize::try_from(sec.raw_size).unwrap_or(0);
                let end = start.saturating_add(size).min(load.data.len());
                if start >= end { continue; }
                let va_base = image_base + sec.virtual_addr;

            "path": path,
            "total": stats.total,
            "by_encoding": stats.by_encoding,
            "avg_length": stats.avg_length,
            "max_length": stats.max_length,
            "interesting_count": stats.interesting_count,
            "classified_count": stats.classified_count,
            "format_string_count": stats.format_string_count,
            "url_count": stats.url_count,
            "path_count": stats.path_count,
            "longest": stats.longest,
            "shortest_interesting": stats.shortest_interesting,
            "source": "rustre_analysis_string::StringStats::compute",
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

// â”€â”€â”€ DWARF: variables / symbol-set summary / unwinder â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€

pub struct DwarfVariablesPathTool;

impl DwarfVariablesPathTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "dwarf_variables_path".to_string(),
            description: "Parse DWARF .debug_info and return top-level variables (name, type, location).".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": { "path": { "type": "string" } },
                "required": ["path"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DwarfVariablesPathTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let path = args.get("path").and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'path'".into()))?;
        let reader = rustre_symbols_dwarf::DwarfReader::open(std::path::Path::new(path))
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("dwarf open failed: {e}")))?;
        let vars = reader.variables();
        let payload = serde_json::to_value(&vars)
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("serialize failed: {e}")))?;
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({ "count": vars.len(), "variables": payload }).to_string()))
    }
}

pub struct DwarfUnwinderAtPathTool;

impl DwarfUnwinderAtPathTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "dwarf_unwinder_at_path".to_string(),
            description: "Parse .eh_frame/.debug_frame from an ELF and return the unwind step covering `pc` (or null).".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": { "type": "string" },
                    "pc": { "type": "integer" }
                },
                "required": ["path", "pc"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DwarfUnwinderAtPathTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let path = args.get("path").and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'path'".into()))?;
        let pc = args.get("pc").and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'pc'".into()))?;
        let raw = std::fs::read(path)
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("read failed: {e}")))?;
        let unw = rustre_symbols_dwarf::DwarfUnwinder::new(&raw)
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("unwinder init failed: {e}")))?;
        let step = unw.unwind_at(pc);
        let payload = serde_json::to_value(&step)
            .map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("serialize failed: {e}")))?;
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({ "pc": pc, "step": payload }).to_string()))
    }
}

pub struct NetDissectIcmpStreamTunnelHeuristicTool;

impl NetDissectIcmpStreamTunnelHeuristicTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "net_dissect_icmp_stream_tunnel_heuristic".to_string(),
            description:
                "Flag whether a stream of ICMP hex payloads looks like a tunnel via \
                 rustre_net_dissect::icmp_stream_tunnel_heuristic."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "payloads": {
                        "type": "array",
                        "items": { "type": "string" }
                    }
                },
                "required": ["payloads"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for NetDissectIcmpStreamTunnelHeuristicTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let arr = args
            .get("payloads")
            .and_then(Value::as_array)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'payloads' array".into()))?;
        let mut decoded: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());
        for v in arr {
            let s = v.as_str().ok_or_else(|| {
                McpError::InvalidParams("payload entries must be hex strings".into())
            })?;
            decoded.push(icmp_tun_hex(s)?);
        }
        let refs: Vec<&[u8]> = decoded.iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
        let tunnel = rustre_net_dissect::icmp_stream_tunnel_heuristic(&refs);
        Ok(ToolResult::text(
            json!({
                "count": refs.len(),
                "tunnel_suspected": tunnel,
                "source": "rustre_net_dissect::icmp_stream_tunnel_heuristic",
            })
            .to_string(),
        ))
    }
}

fn icmp_tun_hex(s: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, McpError> {
    let t: String = s.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
    if t.len() % 2 != 0 {
        return Err(McpError::InvalidParams("hex length must be even".into()));
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(t.len() / 2);
    let bytes = t.as_bytes();
    for i in (0..bytes.len()).step_by(2) {
        let hi = icmp_tun_nib(bytes[i])?;
        let lo = icmp_tun_nib(bytes[i + 1])?;
        out.push((hi << 4) | lo);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

fn icmp_tun_nib(b: u8) -> Result<u8, McpError> {
    match b {
        b'0'..=b'9' => Ok(b - b'0'),
        b'a'..=b'f' => Ok(b - b'a' + 10),
        b'A'..=b'F' => Ok(b - b'A' + 10),
        _ => Err(McpError::InvalidParams("invalid hex digit".into())),
    }
}

// â”€â”€â”€ Extra rustre-db base-migrations wrappers (round N+1) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€

/// Average `up_sql` byte length across `rustre_db::base_migrations()`.
pub struct DbBaseMigrationsAvgSqlBytesTool;

impl DbBaseMigrationsAvgSqlBytesTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "db_base_migrations_avg_sql_bytes".to_string(),
            description:
                "Return the average byte length of `up_sql` across canonical base-schema \
                 migrations from rustre_db::base_migrations()."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({ "type": "object", "properties": {} }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DbBaseMigrationsAvgSqlBytesTool {
    async fn call(&self, _args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let migs = rustre_db::base_migrations();
        let count = migs.len();
        let total: usize = migs.iter().map(|m| m.up_sql.len()).sum();
        #[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss)]
        let avg = if count == 0 { 0.0 } else { total as f64 / count as f64 };
        Ok(ToolResult::text(
            json!({
                "count":       count,
                "total_bytes": total,
                "avg_bytes":   avg,
                "source":      "rustre_db::base_migrations",
            })
            .to_string(),
        ))
    }
}

/// Return the migration with the largest `up_sql` from `rustre_db::base_migrations()`.
pub struct DbBaseMigrationsLargestUpSqlTool;

impl DbBaseMigrationsLargestUpSqlTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "db_base_migrations_largest_up_sql".to_string(),
            description:
                "Return the migration (version, name, size) with the largest `up_sql` from \
                 rustre_db::base_migrations()."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({ "type": "object", "properties": {} }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DbBaseMigrationsLargestUpSqlTool {
    async fn call(&self, _args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let migs = rustre_db::base_migrations();
        let largest = migs.iter().max_by_key(|m| m.up_sql.len());
        let payload = match largest {
            Some(m) => json!({
                "found":     true,
                "version":   m.version.0,
                "name":      m.name,
                "up_bytes":  m.up_sql.len(),
                "source":    "rustre_db::base_migrations",
            }),
            None => json!({
                "found":  false,
                "source": "rustre_db::base_migrations",
            }),
        };
        Ok(ToolResult::text(payload.to_string()))
    }
}

/// Report whether a given migration version exists in `rustre_db::base_migrations()`.
pub struct DbBaseMigrationsHasVersionTool;

impl DbBaseMigrationsHasVersionTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "db_base_migrations_has_version".to_string(),
            description:
                "Return whether a given version is present in the canonical base-schema \
                 migrations from rustre_db::base_migrations()."
                    .to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": { "version": { "type": "integer" } },
                "required": ["version"]
            }),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DbBaseMigrationsHasVersionTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let version = args
            .get("version")
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'version'".to_string()))?;
        let v = u32::try_from(version)
            .map_err(|_| McpError::InvalidParams("'version' out of range".to_string()))?;
        let migs = rustre_db::base_migrations();
        let has = migs.iter().any(|m| m.version.0 == v);
        Ok(ToolResult::text(
            json!({
                "version": v,
                "found":   has,
                "count":   migs.len(),
                "source":  "rustre_db::base_migrations",
            })
            .to_string(),
        ))
    }
}

pub struct ScriptLuaExecuteScriptTool;
impl ScriptLuaExecuteScriptTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "script_lua_execute_script".to_string(),
            description: "Execute a sandboxed Lua-like script via rustre_script_lua::LuaEngine::execute and return the captured print output plus final value.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","required":["script"],"properties":{"script":{"type":"string"},"max_steps":{"type":"integer","minimum":1}}}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for ScriptLuaExecuteScriptTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let script = args.get("script").and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("script: missing/not string".into()))?;
        let mut engine = rustre_script_lua::LuaEngine::new();
        if let Some(n) = args.get("max_steps").and_then(Value::as_u64) {
            engine.set_max_steps(n);
        }
        let mut ctx = rustre_script_lua::LuaContext::new();
        match engine.execute(script, &mut ctx) {
            Ok(v) => Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
                "ok": true,
                "result": v.to_string(),
                "type": v.type_name(),
                "output": ctx.output_text(),
                "steps": engine.step_count(),
                "source": "rustre_script_lua::LuaEngine::execute",
            }).to_string())),
            Err(e) => Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
                "ok": false,
                "error": e.to_string(),
                "output": ctx.output_text(),
                "source": "rustre_script_lua::LuaEngine::execute",
            }).to_string())),
        }
    }
}

pub struct DotnetMetadataParseDirectSummaryTool;
impl DotnetMetadataParseDirectSummaryTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "dotnet_metadata_parse_direct_summary".to_string(),
            description: "Parse a .NET metadata blob (hex) and return aggregate statistics.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","properties":{"data_hex":{"type":"string"}},"required":["data_hex"]}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DotnetMetadataParseDirectSummaryTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let hex = args.get("data_hex").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'data_hex'".into()))?;
        let bytes = libfuzzer_hex_str_to_bytes(hex)?;
        let reader = rustre_dotnet_metadata::parse_metadata_direct(&bytes).map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("parse_metadata_direct: {e}")))?;
        let stats = reader.statistics();
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "string_heap_total_bytes": stats.string_heap_total_bytes,

    }

            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","properties":{"data_hex":{"type":"string"}},"required":["data_hex"]}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DotnetMetadataValidateTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let hex = args.get("data_hex").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'data_hex'".into()))?;
        let bytes = libfuzzer_hex_str_to_bytes(hex)?;

        let issues: Vec<Value> = vr.issues.iter().map(|i| json!({"message": i.message, "is_error": i.is_error})).collect();
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({"is_valid": vr.is_valid(), "issue_count": vr.issue_count(), "issues": issues, "source": "rustre_dotnet_metadata::validate_metadata"}).to_string()))
    }

pub struct DotnetMetadataParseMethodBodyTool;
impl DotnetMetadataParseMethodBodyTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "dotnet_metadata_parse_method_body".to_string(),
            description: "Parse a CIL method body from a raw PE image (hex) at file_offset.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","properties":{"image_hex":{"type":"string"},"file_offset":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}},"required":["image_hex","file_offset"]}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for DotnetMetadataParseMethodBodyTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let hex = args.get("image_hex").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'image_hex'".into()))?;
        let off = args.get("file_offset").and_then(Value::as_u64).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'file_offset'".into()))? as usize;
        let bytes = libfuzzer_hex_str_to_bytes(hex)?;
        let body = rustre_dotnet_metadata::parse_method_body(&bytes, off).map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("parse_method_body: {e}")))?;
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "init_locals": body.init_locals,
            "max_stack": body.max_stack,
            "local_var_sig_token": body.local_var_sig_token,
            "code_size": body.code_size(),
            "exception_clause_count": body.exception_clauses.len(),
            "catch_count": body.catch_clauses().len(),
            "finally_count": body.finally_clauses().len(),
            "has_exception_handlers": body.has_exception_handlers(),
            "source": "rustre_dotnet_metadata::parse_method_body"
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

        let hex = args.get("content_hex").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing content_hex".into()))?;
        let off = args.get("offset").and_then(Value::as_u64).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing offset".into()))?;

            "content_len": gf.content.len(),

pub struct EmuQilingFdTableOpenFdsTool;

    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "emu_qiling_fd_table_open_fds".to_string(),
            description: "Create a default FdTable, optionally open N extra files, and return open_fds() sorted list.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","properties":{"extra_opens":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":32}}}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for EmuQilingFdTableOpenFdsTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let n = args.get("extra_opens").and_then(Value::as_u64).unwrap_or(0);
        let mut t = rustre_emu_qiling::FdTable::new();
        for i in 0..n {
            let gf = rustre_emu_qiling::GuestFile::new(0, format!("/tmp/f{i}"), format!("/tmp/f{i}"), true, false);
            t.open(gf);
        }
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "open_fds": t.open_fds(),
            "len": t.len(),
            "source": "rustre_emu_qiling::FdTable::open_fds"
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

pub struct EmuQilingFdTableLenTool;

    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "emu_qiling_fd_table_len".to_string(),
            description: "Return len() and is_empty() of a fresh FdTable after optional close operations on stdio fds.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","properties":{"close_stdio":{"type":"boolean"}}}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for EmuQilingFdTableLenTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let close = args.get("close_stdio").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false);
        let mut t = rustre_emu_qiling::FdTable::new();
        if close {
            t.close(0);
            t.close(1);
            t.close(2);
        }
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "len": t.len(),
            "is_empty": t.is_empty(),
            "source": "rustre_emu_qiling::FdTable::len"
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

pub struct EmuQilingSyscallCtxArgsTool;
impl EmuQilingSyscallCtxArgsTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "emu_qiling_syscall_ctx_args".to_string(),
            description: "Construct a SyscallCtx and echo back arg0..arg5 accessors.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","required":["nr","args"],"properties":{"nr":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"args":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer"},"minItems":6,"maxItems":6}}}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for EmuQilingSyscallCtxArgsTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let nr = args.get("nr").and_then(Value::as_u64).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing nr".into()))?;
        let a = args.get("args").and_then(Value::as_array).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing args".into()))?;
        if a.len() != 6 { return Err(McpError::InvalidParams("args must have exactly 6 entries".into())); }
        let mut arr = [0u64; 6];
        for (i, v) in a.iter().enumerate() {
            arr[i] = v.as_u64().ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams(format!("args[{i}] not u64")))?;
        }
        let ctx = rustre_emu_qiling::SyscallCtx::new(nr, arr, rustre_emu::EmulatorArch::X86_64, rustre_emu_qiling::OsTarget::Linux);
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "nr": ctx.nr,
            "arg0": ctx.arg0(), "arg1": ctx.arg1(), "arg2": ctx.arg2(),
            "arg3": ctx.arg3(), "arg4": ctx.arg4(), "arg5": ctx.arg5(),
            "source": "rustre_emu_qiling::SyscallCtx"
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

pub struct EmuQilingSyscallResultNotImplRetvalTool;
impl EmuQilingSyscallResultNotImplRetvalTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "emu_qiling_syscall_result_not_impl_retval".to_string(),
            description: "Return retval() for SyscallResult variants Ok(v)/NotImplemented/Fatal.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","required":["variant"],"properties":{"variant":{"type":"string","enum":["ok","not_impl","fatal"]},"value":{"type":"integer"}}}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for EmuQilingSyscallResultNotImplRetvalTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let v = args.get("variant").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing variant".into()))?;
        let r = match v {
            "ok" => rustre_emu_qiling::SyscallResult::Ok(args.get("value").and_then(Value::as_i64).unwrap_or(0)),
            "not_impl" => rustre_emu_qiling::SyscallResult::NotImplemented,
            "fatal" => rustre_emu_qiling::SyscallResult::Fatal("test".into()),
            _ => return Err(McpError::InvalidParams("variant must be ok|not_impl|fatal".into())),
        };
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "variant": v,
            "retval": r.retval(),
            "source": "rustre_emu_qiling::SyscallResult::retval"
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for EmuQilingProcessEnvSetenvCheckTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let k = args.get("key").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing key".into()))?;

        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "key": k,
            "value": v,
            "getenv": got,
            "envp_len": env.envp.len(),
            "source": "rustre_emu_qiling::ProcessEnv::setenv"
        }).to_string()))
    }

pub struct GdbRegisterCodecDecodeGWireTool;
impl GdbRegisterCodecDecodeGWireTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "gdb_register_codec_decode_g".to_string(),
            description: "Decode a 'g' packet hex payload against target.xml.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","properties":{"xml":{"type":"string"},"hex":{"type":"string"}},"required":["xml","hex"]}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for GdbRegisterCodecDecodeGWireTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let xml = args.get("xml").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'xml'".into()))?;
        let hex = args.get("hex").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'hex'".into()))?;
        let t = rustre_debug_gdb::GdbTargetXml::parse(xml).map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("parse: {e}")))?;
        let codec = rustre_debug_gdb::GdbRegisterCodec::new(t.clone());
        let regs = codec.decode_g_packet(hex).map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("decode: {e}")))?;
        let mut map = serde_json::Map::new();
        for r in &t.registers {
            if let Some(v) = regs.get(&r.name) {
                map.insert(r.name.clone(), json!(v));
            }
        }
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "pc": regs.pc,
            "sp": regs.sp,
            "fp": regs.fp,
            "lr": regs.lr,
            "registers": Value::Object(map),
            "source":"rustre_debug_gdb::GdbRegisterCodec::decode_g_packet"
        }).to_string()))
    }
}

pub struct GdbRegisterCodecEncodeGWireTool;
impl GdbRegisterCodecEncodeGWireTool {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn definition() -> ToolDefinition {
        ToolDefinition {
            name: "gdb_register_codec_encode_g".to_string(),
            description: "Encode a register-values map into a 'G' packet payload.".to_string(),
            input_schema: json!({"type":"object","properties":{"xml":{"type":"string"},"values":{"type":"object"}},"required":["xml"]}),
            parameters: Value::Null,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl ToolHandler for GdbRegisterCodecEncodeGWireTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<ToolResult, McpError> {
        let xml = args.get("xml").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or_else(|| McpError::InvalidParams("missing 'xml'".into()))?;
        let t = rustre_debug_gdb::GdbTargetXml::parse(xml).map_err(|e| McpError::InternalError(format!("parse: {e}")))?;
        let codec = rustre_debug_gdb::GdbRegisterCodec::new(t);
        let mut set = rustre_debug::RegisterSet::new();
        if let Some(obj) = args.get("values").and_then(Value::as_object) {
            for (k, v) in obj {
                if let Some(n) = v.as_u64() {
                    set.set(k, n);
                }
            }
        }
        let payload = codec.encode_g_packet(&set);
        Ok(ToolResult::text(json!({
            "payload": payload,
            "length": payload.len(),
            "source":"rustre_debug_gdb::GdbRegisterCodec::encode_g_packet"
        }).to_string()))
    }
}
